paras: The Arcadia, Oklahoma, polling-place confrontation took place on the afternoon of 2 August 1910, when an election inspector at Arcadia drew a revolver and threatened to shoot a group of about 30 Black men lined up at the polls. The crowd dispersed, no one was reported hurt, and the polls were closed until more ballots arrived. The only report found, an Oklahoma City dispatch to the Chickasha Daily Express, presented the incident as a "race riot" narrowly averted.
Arcadia lay about twenty-five miles northeast of Oklahoma City, according to the dispatch. The trouble began during the voting that day, when the election ballots for Republicans were all used up.

According to the dispatch, 30 Black men then lined up at the polls and refused to let Democrats vote until more Republican ballots were obtained so that they could continue voting. The election inspector responded by drawing a revolver and threatening to shoot, and the crowd broke up. The polls were closed at 2:30 until more ballots could be obtained from the state election board.
The coverage names neither the inspector nor any of the men at the polls, and no report of arrests or of any official inquiry was found.

The story ran on the front page of the Chickasha Daily Express on 3 August 1910 as a short "Special to the Express" from Oklahoma City under the headline "RACE RIOT AVERTED." The dispatch credited the "prompt action" of the inspector for preventing a riot and described the Black voters, called "negroes," as the source of the trouble. Its account came entirely from the side of the polling officials; it did not report what the Black men said or whether the Republican voters were able to vote once ballots arrived.
No other white paper and no Black newspaper in the searched collections was found to have reported the incident.

accounts.label: Oklahoma City special dispatch
accounts.gist: Republican ballots ran out, and 30 Black men lined up at the polls to keep Democrats from voting until more arrived; the election inspector broke up the crowd with a drawn revolver, and the polls closed at 2:30 pending ballots from the state election board.

framing.detail: Headline 'RACE RIOT AVERTED' casts the Black voters as the threat and praises the inspector's 'prompt action' in drawing a revolver.

record_check.dossier: The report gives 30 Black men, not about 80
A single election inspector, not police or sheriff's officers
County not stated; the report places Arcadia 25 miles northeast of Oklahoma City
Supported: 'yesterday afternoon' in an Aug. 3 dispatch
